faqs.question: What is a good Diwali shayari for my wife?
faqs.answer: Pick a sher built on a word she would call herself. For a first Diwali together, the Lakshmi couplet about two pairs of hands at the puja altar works; for a long marriage with many moves, the humsafar couplet about lighting the first diya in every rented home. All 12 on this page are original, with Devanagari, Roman and English versions.

faqs.question: What does ardhangini mean, and is it a compliment?
faqs.answer: Wiktionary builds ardhangini (अर्धांगिनी) from ardh (half), ang (part or limb) and a feminine ending, and glosses it as 'better half, wife'. Most wives hear it as warm; the ardhangini sher here turns it round, saying she is not half but the whole of your colour.

faqs.question: Is it okay to call my wife Lakshmi in a Diwali shayari?
faqs.answer: It is traditional: Platts' 1884 dictionary even records a Lakshmi puja done by a bride and groom after the bride reaches her in-laws' home. But some wives hear it as praise for running the house. If she has said so, send the humsafar or shareek-e-hayat lines instead.

faqs.question: Which shayari suits our first Diwali after the wedding?
faqs.answer: The second Lakshmi sher: "Is baar pooja ki chauki par do jodi haath jude, jitne diye jale, sab tumhari hi or mude", meaning two pairs of hands folded at the altar this year and every diya turned towards her. Send it on Friday 29 October 2027, before the Lakshmi Puja.

faqs.question: What does shareek-e-hayat mean?
faqs.answer: It means partner of a life. Platts defines sharīk as a sharer or partner, and hayāt means life. The sher on this page plays on it: the whole neighbourhood shares your joy, but the one who shares your sorrow is your shareek-e-hayat.

faqs.question: Is there a funny Diwali shayari for my wife?
faqs.answer: Yes, the two begum sher. One promises that every light burns at her command and the husband will pay the electricity bill too; the other admits he forgot the whole shopping list and remembered only her smile. Send them only if she enjoys being teased.

faqs.question: Can a wife send these shayari to her husband?
faqs.answer: The two hamdam sher are written for exactly that, with feminine verbs. Platts glosses hamdam as "breathing together" and "a spouse", so it suits a husband. The humsafar lines also work in either direction if you change "meri humsafar" to "mere humsafar".

faqs.question: When is Diwali 2027, and when should I send my wife a shayari?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja falls on Friday 29 October 2027, with Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October and Padwa on Saturday 30 October. Send a Lakshmi sher before the evening puja, a humsafar sher after the aarti, and the Padwa sher the next morning.

faqs.question: What if my wife doesn't read Hindi script?
faqs.answer: Send the Roman version, which is given under every couplet, and add the English line if Hindi is not her first language. The sound of the rhyme survives in Roman script; only the look of the Devanagari is lost.

faqs.question: Do husbands or wives express more affection in Indian marriages?
faqs.answer: In a 2025 BMC Psychology study of 340 married couples in India, husbands scored 8.09 and wives 7.94 on affectional expression, a difference that was not statistically significant. Love-marriage and arranged-marriage couples reported similar levels too.

faqs.question: Where does a shayari go in SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali page?
faqs.answer: Choose "your love" as who it is for, then put one line on the tag of the diya waiting at her door, a wish on each diya in the row, and the full couplet in the letter sealed in the shagun liffafa. You can add up to six photos and an optional password before you send the private link.

# Diwali Shayari for Wife: 12 Original Sher on Six Words for Her

The best Diwali shayari for wife calls her by a word she would choose herself, so here are 12 original sher built on six: Lakshmi, ardhangini, humsafar, shareek-e-hayat, begum and, for a wife writing back, hamdam. Ten are for a wife and two for a husband, each in Devanagari, Roman script and English. Pick one for Lakshmi Puja on Friday, 29 October 2027, or for Padwa the morning after.

Why fuss over one word? On SubhSandesh, the romantic "I love you" page drew 17,093 views, 29.7% of all page views (measured 24 September 2026). And 48.3% of shared pages open on a phone, where a two-line sher fits one screen.

## Six Hindi and Urdu words for a wife, checked in Platts (1884) and Wiktionary

We checked all six in John T. Platts' 1884 *Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English* or in Wiktionary. The meanings are sharper than most forwards assume.

- **Lakshmi (लक्ष्मी).** Platts (p. 959) says [lakshmī-pūjā also means worship "by the bridegroom and bride after the bride has been brought to her father-in-law's house"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%80&searchhws=yes), and lists *Lakshmi ghar mein aana*, fortune coming home.
- **Ardhangini (अर्धांगिनी).** Wiktionary: [अर्ध (half) + अंग (part) + the feminine -इनी: "better half, wife"](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%80).
- **Humsafar (हमसफ़र) and hamdam (हमदम).** Platts (pp. 1233–34) gives [ham-safar as "fellow-traveller" and ham-dam as "lit. 'breathing together'… a spouse"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%D9%87%D9%85&searchhws=yes).
- **Shareek-e-hayat (शरीक-ए-हयात).** Platts (p. 727) defines [sharīk as "a sharer, participator… a partner"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%8A%DA%A9&searchhws=yes); with *hayāt* (life), it means partner of a life.
- **Begum (बेगम).** Platts (p. 210) gives ["Lady; queen: a title of Mogal ladies"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%D8%A8%DB%8C%DA%AF%D9%85&searchhws=yes), which suits teasing better than solemnity.

## 12 original Diwali shayari for wife and husband, one word at a time

Every sher was written for this page and checked against every earlier Diwali post here. Each block gives the couplet, Roman version and English gloss.

### 1. Lakshmi: for Lakshmi Puja night, Friday 29 October 2027

The first uses the idiom of Lakshmi staying. The second suits a first Diwali after the wedding.

> पुरखे कहते थे लक्ष्मी घर में आती है तो रुकती है,\
> तुम्हें आए बारह बरस हुए, ये बात अब सच लगती है।\
> *Purkhe kehte the Lakshmi ghar mein aati hai to rukti hai, / tumhein aaye baarah baras hue, ye baat ab sach lagti hai.*\
> The elders said Lakshmi stays once she comes; twelve years on, I believe them.

> इस बार पूजा की चौकी पर दो जोड़ी हाथ जुड़े,\
> जितने दीये जले, सब तुम्हारी ही ओर मुड़े।\
> *Is baar pooja ki chauki par do jodi haath jude, / jitne diye jale, sab tumhari hi or mude.*\
> Two pairs of hands folded at the altar this year; every diya turned towards you.

### 2. Ardhangini: for the wife who finishes your sentences

Half a body is also half of every conversation. Both suit any length of marriage.

> लोग कहते हैं अर्धांगिनी, आधा अंग हो तुम मेरा,\
> मैं कहता हूँ इस दिवाली, पूरा रंग हो तुम मेरा।\
> *Log kehte hain ardhangini, aadha ang ho tum mera, / main kehta hoon is Diwali, poora rang ho tum mera.*\
> People call you half of my body; I say this Diwali you are the whole of my colour.

> मेरी अर्धांगिनी आधी बात बिन कहे समझ जाती है,\
> बाक़ी आधी कहने को हर साल दिवाली की रात आती है।\
> *Meri ardhangini aadhi baat bin kahe samajh jaati hai, / baaqi aadhi kehne ko har saal Diwali ki raat aati hai.*\
> My other half grasps half of what I mean unsaid; Diwali night comes for the rest.

### 3. Humsafar: for a marriage of many Diwalis and many addresses

These suit couples who have moved cities. Both count the road, not the years.

> कितनी दिवालियाँ बीतीं, कितने शहर, कितने किराए के घर,\
> हर नए आँगन में पहला दीया तुमने रखा, मेरी हमसफ़र।\
> *Kitni Diwaliyan beetin, kitne shehar, kitne kiraaye ke ghar, / har naye aangan mein pehla diya tumne rakha, meri humsafar.*\
> So many Diwalis, cities and rented homes; in each new courtyard you lit the first diya.

> सफ़र में कई अमावसें आईं, कई रातें लंबी थीं,\
> हर बार हाथ थामने वाली उँगलियाँ तुम्हारी ही थीं।\
> *Safar mein kai amaavasein aayin, kai raatein lambi thin, / har baar haath thaamne waali ungliyan tumhari hi thin.*\
> The road had many moonless, long nights; each time, the fingers holding my hand were yours.

### 4. Shareek-e-hayat: for Padwa morning, Saturday 30 October 2027

Many Marathi homes keep Padwa as a day for husband and wife; in Gujarat it is the new year. The second sher is for the quiet morning.

> ख़ुशी में शरीक तो सारा मोहल्ला हो जाता है,\
> जो ग़म में भी शरीक रहे, शरीक-ए-हयात कहलाता है।\
> *Khushi mein shareek to saara mohalla ho jaata hai, / jo gham mein bhi shareek rahe, shareek-e-hayaat kehlaata hai.*\
> The neighbourhood shares your joy; whoever shares your sorrow is your life's partner.

> पड़वा की सुबह, कल की बची मिठाई, तुम्हारी चाय की प्याली,\
> शोर थम गया तो पता चला, यही थी मेरी असली दिवाली।\
> *Padwa ki subah, kal ki bachi mithai, tumhari chai ki pyaali, / shor tham gaya to pata chala, yahi thi meri asli Diwali.*\
> Padwa morning, leftover sweets, your tea; once the noise stopped, this was my real Diwali.

### 5. Begum: two playful sher for a wife who laughs first

"Lady; queen" makes begum a teasing word. Send these only if she enjoys that.

> बेगम, आपके हुक्म पर आज हर लड़ी, हर दीया जलेगा,\
> बिजली का बिल जब आएगा, वो भी ये ग़ुलाम ही भरेगा।\
> *Begum, aapke hukm par aaj har ladi, har diya jalega, / bijli ka bill jab aayega, wo bhi ye ghulaam hi bharega.*\
> Begum, every light burns at your command tonight; this servant will pay the electricity bill too.

> बेगम ने सामान की सूची दी, हमने रास्ते भर दोहराई,\
> दुकान पहुँचे तो उस सूची में बस उनकी मुस्कान याद आई।\
> *Begum ne saamaan ki soochi di, humne raaste bhar dohraai, / dukaan pahunche to us soochi mein bas unki muskaan yaad aayi.*\
> Begum gave me a shopping list; at the shop I remembered only her smile.

### 6. Hamdam: two sher from a wife to her husband

Hamdam means "breathing together", so it fits a husband too. The verbs are feminine, for a wife to send.

> हमदम, आज की भीड़ में भी तुम्हारी आहट पहचानती हूँ,\
> सौ दीयों के बीच तुम्हारी लौ अलग से जानती हूँ।\
> *Humdum, aaj ki bheed mein bhi tumhari aahat pehchaanti hoon, / sau diyon ke beech tumhari lau alag se jaanti hoon.*\
> My hamdam, even in tonight's crowd I know your footsteps; among a hundred diyas I can tell your flame.

> तुम्हारे बालों में चाँदी उतरी, मैंने धनतेरस का धन पाया,\
> जितनी दिवालियाँ साथ गिनीं, उतना ही ये रिश्ता सवाया।\
> *Tumhare baalon mein chaandi utri, maine Dhanteras ka dhan paaya, / jitni Diwaliyan saath ginin, utna hi ye rishta savaaya.*\
> Silver came into your hair, my Dhanteras wealth; each Diwali together made us a quarter richer.

## Which sher for which marriage, 27–31 October 2027

The right word depends on your marriage and her humour. Figures are platform-wide (24 September 2026); no Diwali data exists yet, so Raksha Bandhan is our nearest festival.

| Your marriage | Sher | When (2027) | SubhSandesh figure behind it |
|---|---|---|---|
| First Diwali together | Lakshmi 2 | Fri 29 Oct, before puja | 48.3% of pages open on a phone: two lines fit |
| Ten-plus years, many moves | Humsafar 1 | Fri 29 Oct, after aarti | 11.1 views per page: she will reread it |
| She likes being teased | Begum 1 | Wed 27 Oct, Dhanteras | 38.5% of creators add a password: keep jokes private |
| Your home keeps Padwa | Shareek-e-hayat 2 | Sat 30 Oct, morning | 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were made on the day (n = 89): write it the night before |

## What 340 Indian couples reported about showing affection (BMC Psychology, 2025)

If yours was an arranged marriage, the evidence is on your side. Kanth and Indumathy's [2025 validation of a Tamil Dyadic Adjustment Scale](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12255064) surveyed 340 married couples in India: 680 people, 65.15% in arranged marriages and 32.79% in love marriages.

Husbands scored 8.09 and wives 7.94 on affectional expression, not a significant difference (p = 0.71), and love and arranged marriages reported similar levels. The study measured marital adjustment, not poetry, so the licence to send a sher is our inference.

## Sending it in SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali card, in "your love" mode

In WhatsApp, a sher drowns among forwards. SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali page gives it a setting: choose "your love" and the default wishes and blessing change to suit a partner. Put one misra on the tag of the diya at her door and the full couplet in the letter inside the shagun liffafa.

Add up to six photos to the sky lanterns and your initials to the rangoli; it takes about five minutes and opens in any browser, no app or account. [Make an interactive Diwali card for your wife with the Happy Diwali template](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali), with an optional password if in-laws share her phone.

For a love note without festival props, try the [Darling romantic page](https://subhsandesh.in/darling), a dark, dramatic page for a partner (457 made by 24 September 2026). It is not a Diwali template, so the sher carries the festival alone.

## When Lakshmi or begum is the wrong word: 3 cases

Not every word suits every wife, and a link is not always right. Here are three cases, one against our own product.

- **She does not want to be the household goddess.** Lakshmi can read as praise for running the home: a job, not a compliment. Send the humsafar lines instead.
- **Your home does not keep Lakshmi Puja.** For Jain, Sikh or interfaith couples, 29 October 2027 may mean Mahavira's nirvana or Bandi Chhor Divas. The humsafar lines carry no ritual.
- **She is in the same room.** If you are both home, a handwritten sher tucked into her mithai box beats any link, ours included.

- Wiktionary, अर्धांगिनी (Hindi), checked 22 October 2026.
- Kanth and Indumathy, Tamil Dyadic Adjustment Scale, *BMC Psychology*, 11 July 2025.

Angle sharpened accordingly: married-spouse vocabulary (six dictionary-checked words for a wife), Padwa and first-Diwali-after-wedding moments, two sher for a husband, arranged-vs-love-marriage evidence; no Diwali-day timeline (b1's frame), no tum/aap/jaan register section, no voice-note or status section. b1's primary keyword is not retargeted.

structuralLimitations: Cannibalisation gate met: 5 of 10 DuckDuckGo India URLs are shared with b1 diwali-shayari-for-love's recorded SERP (both are generic Diwali-shayari aggregators that rank for any Diwali shayari query). Angle sharpened as recorded in serp.note; the overlap is a property of a thin SERP, not of this post's intent, but Google may still treat the two posts as near-neighbours.

SERP is DuckDuckGo HTML (kl=in-en), lower confidence than a Google India SERP; WebSearch is US-indexed and returned no positions. Top 5 fetched in full with ctx_execute fetch; #6–#10 judged from snippets; scoopwhoop returned 404.

No Diwali usage data exists (/happy-diwali is new). First-party figures are platform-wide (24 Sep 2026) and the Raksha Bandhan 2026 lead-time analogue (n = 89), labelled as such in the body; the table column of SubhSandesh figures is platform-wide and does not vary by marriage type.

Kanth & Indumathy (2025) is a Tamil-language scale validation, mainly from Tamil Nadu, measuring marital adjustment, not poetry or Diwali; the body labels the step to "send a sher" as our inference. CC BY-NC-ND: figures quoted, no table reproduced.

Platts has no headword for ardhangini, hamsafar as one word, hamdam as one word, grihalakshmi or sajni; ham-safar and ham-dam were found under the هم entry (pp. 1233–34), and ardhangini was verified in Wiktionary instead. dsal.uchicago.edu and en.wiktionary.org are cap-exempt reference instruments; Platts is also cited by sibling posts with different entries.

Padwa (30 Oct 2027) is stated only as the day after Lakshmi Puja, per the BRIEF-verified Govardhan/Gujarati New Year date; regional customs (Marathi Diwali Padwa, Gujarati new year) are stated generally without a citation.

Line originality: all 12 couplets (Devanagari and Roman) checked by 4-word n-gram against every blog JSON in content/batches (all batches) and the five fetched competitor pages; the only matches were generic English gloss phrases ('two pairs of hands', 'string of lights and', since cut). b1 diwali-wishes-for-wife uses the word humsafar in a different line; b1 diwali-wishes-for-husband's sajan was avoided.
Search budget: 2 of 3 used (1 WebSearch, 1 DuckDuckGo). Wikipedia: 0 body links; sameAs entities verified via the Wikipedia API (pageprops wikibase_item) on 2026-10-22.

passed: At least 3 first-party facts appear, and at least 2 are in the first 150 words
The post contains at least one claim none of the top 5 pages make
The angle statement is honestly answerable: "wins by being the only post that ___"
No section closely mirrors a competitor page's structure or framing
Direct answer in the first 150 words, before any context-setting
Every H2 section answerable standalone in 2–3 sentences
Paragraphs 2–3 sentences throughout
At least one specific number, date, price or named source per H2 section
One comparison table with real values, 3–5 rows
FAQ with 8–12 naturally phrased questions
FAQs appear ONLY in article.faqs and the FAQPage JSON-LD, never in contentMarkdown
H2s map to the fan-out sub-queries identified in Phase 2
Target keyword in H1, metaTitle, slug, and first 100 words
metaTitle 50–60 characters, exact keyword in the first five words (hard cap 70)
metaTitle differs from the H1, uses one separator, and carries a differentiator no competitor could claim
No banned booster in metaTitle (Best, Top, Ultimate, Complete Guide, Everything You Need to Know)
No year-stamp on an evergreen title; no brand suffix; one keyword only
metaDescription 150–160 characters (hard cap 170)
metaDescription leads with the answer, carries the keyword near the start and at least one number, and has no CTA cliché
excerpt under 300 characters
Exactly one H1; no skipped heading levels
1,500–1,800 words in contentMarkdown excluding FAQs, no padding
Slug short, hyphenated, lowercase, no stop words
Slug is not already taken in Strapi
3–6 outbound links, all fetched and verified to contain the cited fact
Every outbound fact passes the "would it stay without the link" test
Zero competitor links
Wikipedia links: 0–2, entities only
2–4 internal links with descriptive anchor text, placed after value is established
Every internal link is a real URL from TEMPLATE_LINKS
At least 2 sources pass the **subject test** — about siblings / ritual / distance / the language / the platform behaviour, not merely about India or the internet
At least 1 of those is peer-reviewed or scholarly, and open-access
No source passes the **swap test** — none could sit unchanged in a different keyword's post in this batch
At most 1 generic context statistic (PIB / TRAI / Census / MEA)

No source URL appears in more than 2 posts in this batch; no domain in more than 3. **One exception: the date/festival reference** (e.g. a panchang for the festival date and muhurat). Every post in a festival batch may verify the same date — that is a fact-check, not a citation, and it has no cap. It only earns a place in `citation` where the post actually states the time; a post that merely mentions the date keeps it out of `sources` and `citation` entirely.
Any paywalled citation records that only the abstract was read
No figure, chart, table or substantial passage reproduced from a source
Sources list with publication dates, omitted where the source publishes none
At least one section naming a downside, limit, or case where SubhSandesh loses
keyTakeaways present, 3–5 bullets, each standalone with a number where possible
structuredData contains no type the renderer already builds, except an @id-matched enrichment block on <canonicalURL>#post
The enrichment block carries citation mirroring batchMeta.sources one-to-one, plus about and mentions
Every sameAs in about/mentions verified against the Wikipedia API with its Wikidata QID paired
An ItemList is present if the body ranks or numbers things, mirroring the H3s in the same order
No AggregateRating, Review or HowTo anywhere in structuredData
article.faqs drives the FAQPage the renderer builds, and matches it exactly
categorySlug matches a real Strapi category slug
templateUrls all exist in TEMPLATE_LINKS
Batch JSON validates against references/article-json-schema.md
At least one table column uses first-party data
auditReport.honestAssessment: The measured India top 10 for this query is generic Diwali-shayari aggregators plus one non-Diwali wife page; none offers Diwali shayari addressed to a wife, so this is the only page with original wife (and husband) couplets in three scripts, each anchored in a dictionary-checked word for a spouse, plus Indian evidence that arranged and love marriages express affection alike. It still sits on a low-authority domain, shares 5 SERP URLs with our own b1 love-shayari post (cannibalisation risk), and its first-party data is platform-wide rather than Diwali-specific, so expect months, not weeks.
